en: Jose Rizal wrote the novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose the abuses of the Spanish colonial government.
The critically endangered Philippine eagle, locally called the monkey-eating eagle, serves as the national bird of the Philippines.
The Supreme Court of the Philippines, located in Manila, holds the highest judicial power of the national government.
The Ifugao people carved the famous Banaue Rice Terraces into the Cordillera mountains over two thousand years ago.
The Sinulog Festival in Cebu City honors the Santo Niño with vibrant street dancing every third Sunday of January.
Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator for premature babies to provide affordable healthcare in rural Philippine areas.
General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, at his ancestral home in Kawit, Cavite.
Filipino, primarily based on Tagalog, and English are the two official languages used in Philippine government and schools.
The sampaguita, a small white flower with a sweet fragrance, was declared the national flower of the Philippines in 1934.
Every eligible Filipino citizen has the civic duty to vote during national and local elections to choose government leaders.
The Filipino value of bayanihan involves community members working together to physically carry and move a traditional nipa hut.
National Artist Fernando Amorsolo is famous for his paintings depicting rural Philippine landscapes bathed in bright, golden sunlight.
